passage.title: Protecting People in War
paras: In 1859 a Swiss businessman, Henri Dunant, came upon the aftermath of the Battle of Solferino in northern Italy. Thousands of wounded soldiers had been left with almost no care. Shocked, Dunant organised local people to help, and later wrote a book about what he had seen.

His work led to the founding of the Red Cross in 1863 and, in 1864, to the first Geneva Convention, an agreement between states to care for wounded soldiers whoever they fought for. Today the four Geneva Conventions of 1949, and the rules that grew from them, are known as international humanitarian law.

The International Committee of the Red Cross explains that this law has one purpose: to limit the suffering caused by war. It does not decide whether a war is right. It sets rules for how war is fought.

Its key protections are simple to state. Civilians who are not fighting must never be targeted. Attacks must not cause harm to civilians that is excessive compared with the military aim. Wounded and sick fighters must be cared for, and prisoners must be treated humanely. Medical workers and hospitals, marked with the red cross or red crescent, must be respected.
Laws are broken, sometimes terribly. But they give courts, journalists and the public a clear standard by which to hold leaders to account.

questions.q: Core: in the portal response box, write a 60-word summary of the article, then one PEEDL paragraph: 'Which of our poems shows most clearly why such laws are needed?' Starter: 'The law protects..., and [poem] shows...'

questions.q: Extend: compare the law with Islam's rules of conduct from last week
questions.a: Both protect non-combatants; Islam's limits come from revelation and conscience before Allah, the law from treaties between states.

questions.q: Stretch: why might laws fail in practice, and what can still be done?
questions.a: Leaders may ignore them; courts, reporting and public pressure can hold them to account.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of international humanitarian law?
options: to limit the effects of war and protect people
questions.a: B) to limit the effects of war and protect people. It limits suffering in war; it does not decide whether a war is just.
